newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Meeting set on MIM coal mine dispute.
newsitem.headline: Meeting set on MIM coal mine dispute.

text.p: The Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) has convened a meeting on Wednesday between MIM Holdings Ltd and workers at its Oaky Creek coal mine in Queensland following a stand-down of 150 mine workers, a union official said on Monday.

Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) president John Maitland said the miners had been ordered away from the Oaky Creek Number One underground mine for insisting on pre-start safety checks on mine personnel transport vehicles.
CFMEU members had earlier rejected an Oaky Creek management proposal for a new enterprise bargaining agreement.
"If the company wishes to avoid significant embarrasment on this safety issue, they should reach agreement with our members quickly," Maitland told Reuters.
Oaky Creek, a 3.9 million tonne-a-year coking coal operation near Gladstone in north Queensland, employs about 370 workers.
The project includes an open-cut mine which has not been affected by the dispute.
MIM officials were not immediately available for comment.
